description: Erection of a two storey residential house with associated landscaping, private amenity space, cycle and refuse storage.
decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.
Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [P.M.700(B), Planning statement, Preliminary Ecological Appraisal & Preliminary Roost Assessment (prepared by Arbtech), BNG Assessment (prepared by Arbtech), Title deed details for garages to the rear � Received 19/02/2026; Energy statement (ref: 6872, issue 1, dtd Jan 2026, by T16 Design), BNG metric- Received 03/03/2026; Sustainable Drainage assessment (ref: 90937R1, dtd 02/04/2026, by GeoSmart), Sustainable Drainage Proforma- Received 16/04/2026; P.M.000(F), P.M.100(M), P.M.200(G), P.M.300(E), P.M.400(N), P.M.401(H), P.M.500(I), P.M.600(H), Fire safety report- Received 25/06/2026].
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.
Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.
Condition : 4 - No additional windows or openings shall be formed in the side elevation of the new house hereby permitted.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' privacy.
Condition : 5 - All rainwater pipes, gutters, and associated fittings serving the existing and proposed dwellings hereby permitted shall be retained and thereafter maintained within the respective curtilage of each property. At no time shall any such features be positioned so as to discharge onto, overhang, or encroach upon adjoining land.
Reason:
To ensure that drainage arrangements are appropriately contained within the site, to safeguard neighbouring amenity, and to prevent any adverse impacts arising from surface water run-off, in accordance with good planning practice.
Condition : 6 - a)	The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy and shall be retained thereafter for the lifetime of the development.
b)	Prior to first occupation of the new dwelling hereby approved, the relevant evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure/National Calculation Method) shall be submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy, and any subsequent approved revisions. Where a contribution is found necessary to achieve compliance with zero-carbon requirements of the Development Plan, the developer shall have entered into a binding agreement with the Local Planning Authority to pay any carbon offset contribution at the published rate in-force at the time of submitting details pursuant to Part A of this condition. 
Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 7 - (A) No development above ground level shall take place until details have been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority which demonstrate that:
(i)	At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification.
(ii)	At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.
(iii)	No construction or insulation materials are to be used which would release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone.
(B) The development shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of installation contracts) has been submitted to the local planning authority to demonstrate that the development has been carried out in accordance with the approved details under Part A of this condition. The development shall be maintained in accordance with the approved details at all times thereafter.
Reason: In the interests of sustainable development.
Condition : 8 - Prior to first occupation of the building(s) hereby approved, the development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.
Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.
Condition : 9 - 1) Prior to the commencement of development, (excluding demolition and site clearance), details of the final design of a surface water drainage scheme have been submitted to and approved in writing by the planning authority. The design must satisfy the SuDS Hierarchy and be compliant with the National Standards for SuDS, NPPF and Ministerial Statement on SuDS. The required drainage details shall include:
a. Infiltration testing, which shall be carried out in accordance with BRE Digest 365 and confirmation of groundwater levels. Where infiltration is proposed confirmation is required of a 1m unsaturated zone from the base of any proposed soakaway to the seasonal high groundwater level and confirmation of half-drain times. 
b. Hydraulic calculations to demonstrate the proposed final solution will effectively manage the 1 in 30 (+30% allowance for climate change) 1 in 100 (+40% allowance for climate change) storm events and 10% allowance for urban creep. If infiltration is deemed unfeasible, associated discharge rates and storage volumes shall be provided using a maximum discharge rate of 1L/s.
c. Detailed design drawings for all sustainable drainage elements including cross sections and detailed drainage layout plan.
d. An exceedance flow routing plan demonstrating no increase in surface water flood risk on or off site. The plan must include proposed levels and flow directions.
Reasons: To provide a sustainable development and to comply with Policies EQ3 of the Hounslow Local Plan and guidance within the NPPF
Informative: The current strategy does not show exceedance flow routes and the plans do not show the proposed drainage elements (soakaway and planters/water butts). As per the condition, these should be included in the version submitted to discharge the condition.
Condition : 10 - Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development, a Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, the Plan shall include;
(a) information about the steps taken or to be taken to minimise the adverse effect of the development on the biodiversity of the onsite habitat and any other habitat,
(b) the pre-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(c) the post-development biodiversity value of the onsite habitat,
(d) any registered offsite biodiversity gain allocated to the development and the biodiversity value of that gain in relation to the development,
(e) any biodiversity credits purchased for the development, and
(f) such other matters as the Secretary of State may by regulations specify.
The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan prior to the first occupation of the development. Any habitats created or enhanced on-site and off-site in accordance with the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be maintained thereafter for a minimum of 30 years.
Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 11 - A) Prior to the first commencement of the hereby approved development a Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) prepared in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include:
(i) a non-technical summary;
(ii) the roles and responsibilities of the people or organisation(s) delivering the HMMP
(iii) the planned habitat creation and enhancement works to create or improve habitat to achieve the biodiversity net gain in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan;
(iv) the management measures to maintain habitat in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Gain Plan for a period of 30 years from the completion of development; and 
(v) the monitoring methodology and frequency in respect of the created or enhanced habitat to be submitted to the local planning authority. 

B) No occupation or use of the hereby approved development shall take place until:
(i) the habitat creation and enhancement works set out in the approved HMMP have been completed; and 
(ii) a completion report, evidencing the completed habitat enhancements, has been submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. 
The created and/or enhanced habitat specified in the approved HMMP shall be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved HMMP.

C) Monitoring reports shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority in writing in accordance with the methodology and frequency specified in the approved HMMP.

Reason. In the interests of improving Biodiversity and in accordance with The Town and Country Planning Act 1990, Section 90A, Schedule 7A.
Condition : 12 - The development shall be carried out in accordance with the recommendations of the approved Preliminary Ecological Appraisal and Preliminary Roost Assessment. This shall include:
a)	the completion of any further bat surveys identified as necessary prior to works affecting potential bat roosting features and the implementation of any resultant mitigation, compensation, lighting or licensing requirements;
b)	measures to safeguard nesting birds during vegetation clearance and construction works;
c)	the implementation of precautionary working methods for reptiles and small mammals during site clearance and construction; and
d)	the provision of biodiversity enhancement measures recommended within the approved assessment.
Where ecological surveys, supervision, mitigation or licensing are identified as necessary, such measures shall be undertaken with the involvement of suitably qualified specialists. All ecological protection, mitigation and enhancement measures shall be retained thereafter where applicable.
Reason: To protect biodiversity and safeguarded species and to secure ecological enhancements.
Condition : 13 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved landscape details including boundary treatment (dwg ref P.M.401(H)).
The landscaping works shall comply with the requirements specified in BS 3936 (1992) 'Specification of Nursery Stock Part 1 Trees and Shrubs', and in BS 4428 (1989) 'Recommendations for General Landscape Operations', and shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use.
Reason: In order to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site, surrounding area and to promote biodiversity.
Condition : 14 - Prior to the first occupation of the dwelling hereby approved, secure and covered cycle parking facilities for a minimum of two bicycles shall be provided in accordance with the standards set out in the West London Cycle Parking Guidance. The cycle parking facilities shall be retained thereafter for unobstructed use.
Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 15 - Prior to first occupation, the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans, including the removal of the existing dropped kerb to the front of the site and the reinstatement of the footway and kerb and shall be retained thereafter.
Reason: To ensure a safe and convenient environment for pedestrians and to safeguard the character and function of the highway.
Condition : 16 - Before the new dwelling hereby approved is first occupied, the developer shall provide to each dwelling a set of containers required at the time of development for household use for the storage and collection of recyclable materials for the purposes of the Council's kerbside recycling service, to the specification then in use by the local authority's recycling collection service and shall notify the Council's refuse and recycling services when the development is first occupied.  The waste and recyclable materials containers shall be stored in a proprietary refuse bin enclosure designed for the purpose to be supplied by the developer and located such that the distance between the refuse and recycling store and the kerbside collection point does not exceed 15 metres. Each dwelling with a private garden shall also be supplied with a garden waste composting bin of at least 220 litres capacity at the same time.
Reason: In order to protect the quality of the local environment and neighbours' living conditions and to endure appropriate means of refuse storage are provided.
